nullref.title: NullReferenceException
nullref.short: A member was accessed through a null reference.
nullref.summary: A property or method is being used on a reference that does not point to an object.
nullref.why: name does not refer to any String object, so its Length property cannot be read.
nullref.tips: Check the stack-trace line number, then inspect values on that line that could be null.

badNotes.2: name may be null but is being dereferenced

goodNotes.3: Check that the value is not null first

cs0103.title: CS0103
cs0103.short: The name does not exist in the current context.
cs0103.summary: A variable, method, or other name is being referenced from a place where it has not been declared or is not visible.
cs0103.why: The compiler cannot find a name called score in the current scope.
cs0103.tips: Check spelling, where the declaration appears, and whether the reference is inside the correct braces.

badNotes.1: score has not been declared yet

key-not-found.title: KeyNotFoundException
key-not-found.short: A missing Dictionary key was accessed directly.
key-not-found.summary: The indexer [] is being used to read a key that is not present in the Dictionary.
key-not-found.why: Dictionary lookup through [] throws when the requested key does not exist.
key-not-found.tips: Use TryGetValue when the key is not guaranteed to exist.

badNotes.2: A missing key causes an exception here

goodNotes.1: TryGetValue checks existence and retrieves the value together

dict-safe.title: Safely get a value from a Dictionary
dict-safe.short: Use TryGetValue for keys that may not exist.
dict-safe.summary: When a key may be absent, TryGetValue is usually safer than reading it directly with [].
dict-safe.why: TryGetValue performs the lookup and retrieval together and returns false when the key is not found.
dict-safe.tips: It is usually clearer than calling ContainsKey and then indexing with [].

json-read.title: Read a JSON file
json-read.short: Convert JSON to a C# object with System.Text.Json.
json-read.summary: This is the basic pattern for reading a JSON string and converting it to a C# type.
json-read.why: File.ReadAllText reads the file as a string, and JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T> converts that string to the requested type.
json-read.tips: If JSON property names differ from C# property names, use the JsonPropertyName attribute.

int-div.title: Integer division
int-div.short: A calculation expected to produce 0.5 instead produces 0.
int-div.summary: Using / with two int values performs integer division and discards the fractional part. No exception or warning is produced.
int-div.why: Even if the destination is double, a / b is evaluated as int division before the result is assigned.
int-div.tips: Because the program still runs, this kind of bug can be harder to notice than an exception.

badNotes.3: Both operands are int, so this is integer division

goodNotes.1: Convert one operand to double before dividing

nullable.title: null and nullable reference types
nullable.short: Understand the difference between string and string?.
nullable.summary: With nullable reference types enabled, C# can distinguish references that allow null from references that are intended not to be null.
nullable.why: The compiler tracks possible null values and can warn about potentially unsafe dereferences.
nullable.tips: The ! operator is an assertion to the compiler; it does not make a value safer at runtime.

scope.title: Scope
scope.short: The region where a variable or name can be used.
scope.summary: A variable can only be referenced within its defined scope, such as inside the block where it was declared.
scope.why: Limiting where names are visible helps prevent collisions and unintended references to unrelated variables.
scope.tips: When you see CS0103, checking the variable's scope is often a good first step.

index-out-of-range.title: IndexOutOfRangeException
index-out-of-range.short: An array element outside the valid index range was accessed.
index-out-of-range.summary: Valid array indices run from 0 through Length - 1.
index-out-of-range.why: An array with three elements has valid indices 0, 1, and 2. Index 3 is outside the array.
index-out-of-range.tips: Check whether a for-loop condition accidentally uses i <= a.Length.

goodNotes.2: The last valid index is Length - 1

format-exception.title: FormatException
format-exception.short: A string was not in a valid format for the requested conversion.
format-exception.summary: This occurs when methods such as Parse are given text that does not match the expected format.
format-exception.why: The text abc cannot be interpreted as an integer, so int.Parse fails.
format-exception.tips: For user input and other values that may be invalid, TryParse is often a better fit.

badNotes.1: abc cannot be interpreted as an int

goodNotes.1: Use TryParse for input that may fail to convert

parse-number.title: Safely convert a string to a number
parse-number.short: Use TryParse to check whether conversion succeeds.
parse-number.summary: When input is not guaranteed to be numeric, TryParse is usually easier to handle than Parse.
parse-number.why: TryParse returns false instead of throwing an exception when conversion fails.
parse-number.tips: Other types provide similar methods, such as double.TryParse and DateTime.TryParse.

file-not-found.title: FileNotFoundException
file-not-found.short: The file being opened could not be found.
file-not-found.summary: This occurs when no file exists at the specified path.
file-not-found.why: Relative paths are resolved from the process's current working directory, which may not be the directory you expected.
file-not-found.tips: Print Path.GetFullPath(path) to see the exact location the program is trying to use.

badNotes.1: This reads a path that may not exist

goodNotes.2: Check that the file exists before reading it

file-read.title: Read a text file
file-read.short: Use File.ReadAllText to read an entire file as a string.
file-read.summary: This is the simplest way to read a small text file in one operation.
file-read.why: File.ReadAllText opens the file, returns all of its text, and closes it automatically.
file-read.tips: For very large files, consider ReadLines or StreamReader so you can process the content incrementally.

json-exception.title: JsonException
json-exception.short: The JSON syntax or value shape does not match what was expected.
json-exception.summary: System.Text.Json throws this when it cannot parse or convert the input JSON correctly.
json-exception.why: It can happen because the JSON itself is invalid or because a JSON value cannot be converted to the requested C# type.
json-exception.tips: The Path and BytePositionInLine values in the exception can help narrow down the problem location.

badNotes.1: The JSON shape does not match the target int type

goodNotes.1: Provide JSON that can be read as an int

cs0029.title: CS0029
cs0029.short: One type cannot be implicitly converted to another.
cs0029.summary: The source and destination types do not match, and C# has no implicit conversion between them.
cs0029.why: string and int are different types, and C# does not automatically interpret a string's contents as a number.
cs0029.tips: Check the types involved and decide whether parsing, casting, or another conversion method is appropriate.

badNotes.1: A string cannot be assigned directly to an int

goodNotes.1: Convert the string to a number explicitly

cs0246.title: CS0246
cs0246.short: A type or namespace name could not be found.
cs0246.summary: Check the type name, using directives, referenced assemblies, and required NuGet packages.
cs0246.why: The compiler cannot resolve that type or namespace from the current compilation.
cs0246.tips: An IDE may offer to add a using directive automatically, but the required package or assembly may also be missing.

badNotes.1: JsonSerializer cannot be resolved from the current namespace imports

goodNotes.1: Import the required namespace with using

using-directive.title: using directives
using-directive.short: Write type names without repeating their namespace.
using-directive.summary: A using directive does not load a type at runtime; it lets source code omit a namespace prefix.
using-directive.why: With using System.Text.Json;, System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer can be written as JsonSerializer.
using-directive.tips: Adding a using directive cannot make a type available if the required assembly or NuGet package is not referenced.

cs8602.title: CS8602
cs8602.short: A possibly null reference is being dereferenced.
cs8602.summary: Nullable analysis has determined that this value may be null.
cs8602.why: Because the code could produce a NullReferenceException at runtime, the compiler warns before execution.
cs8602.tips: Prefer a real null check or a design change instead of silencing the warning with ! without justification.

badNotes.2: A reference that may be null is dereferenced here

goodNotes.2: Verify that the reference is not null before using it

for-loop.title: for-loop boundaries
for-loop.short: Confusing < and <= can easily cause out-of-range access.
for-loop.summary: To iterate through an array from the first element to the last, the usual condition is i < array.Length.
for-loop.why: The last valid index is Length - 1, so allowing i == Length goes one element too far.
for-loop.tips: For a simple traversal of every element, foreach is also worth considering.

badNotes.1: This allows i to reach Length

goodNotes.1: Use i < Length to stay inside the valid range
